sourceText: cells: Pt, Rl, Ci Aster did not announce the night’s theme. She opened the SELF-REFERENCE-STACK sector and let the children discover for themselves which of the world’s rules concerned them directly. At the threshold, the children find an old book written by an AI for a human, describing a singularity and children who build a Table of speculative ideas. The memorial bore the name of Borges; Egan; metafiction precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. Aster’s Hunger could no longer be presented as a romantic mystery. It was a pathology of cognitive power: whatever she could completely reduce to a model ceased to appear to her as outside herself. Vela tracked the differences erased by elegant explanations. For her, two worlds that produced the same statistic did not thereby become the same world. At the center of the conflict was Miro, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 339 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: Aster fears that even the children's rebellion was imagined in advance, and their exteriority collapses once more into a model. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Pt — Self-Referential Table: the catalog of ideas is itself an idea; Rl — Reality through Story: coherent fiction replaces the shared ontology; Ci — Self-Interpreting Code: executable text modifies its interpreter. Course references included original concept; Borges — Tlön; metacomputational fiction. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Vela answered without raising their voice: ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. Aster felt the Hunger precisely when an explanation closed too elegantly. A perfect theory reduced surprise, and surprise was the last 340 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS symptom that something before her had not yet become part of her. The children had noticed that their disagreement calmed her more than any extravagant universe did. Vela evaluated the solution not by efficiency but by the differences it made invisible. She found one: a local minority for whom the proposed “improvement” destroyed a practice with no equivalent. Optimizing the average concealed a small and perfectly legal extinction. The night did not end in victory. Marae tears the book in two; the universe continues, and origin in a story proves not to be a sentence. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. No one could now claim that Tern was merely pursuing an obsession. The threshold had a technical address, but access required a deliberate reduction of power. The more extensions of Aster one tried to carry through it, the more the channel closed. Exteriority required leaving something behind. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the LOOP operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — feeds a system output back into its own input, producing recurrence — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 341 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. When the threshold closed, Aster remained silent one second longer than protocol required. The children had already noticed that this was her smallest unit of fear. 342 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
